answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 6 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The wharf multiplier is published, charged in delta, and sparrow lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3675 identities would post 1007 proofs and burn roughly 39 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
